verses.1: After these words and truths, Sanherib became the king of Assyria. He came to Judah and attacked the fortified cities there. He said to the people, “Come out!”
verses.2: And Jehizkiah saw that Sanherib had come, and his face was turned towards the battle against Jerusalem.
verses.3: And he urged his servants and officials to stop the days of suffering that befell them, as they were far away from the city. They helped him out.
verses.4: And they gathered a large number of people together. They blocked all the streams that flowed through the land, saying, “Why do the kings of Assyria come here?” And they found many waters.
verses.5: And he strengthened and built all the cities that had been destroyed. He also built towers on the hills, and he strengthened the walls of David’s city. He also sent many people to attack those cities.
verses.6: And the commanders of the army took them away from the people. They brought them to the gate of the city. There, they spoke to them face to face, saying:
verses.7: Be strong and courageous! Do not fear the king of Assyria, nor any of his army. For we have more power than they do.
verses.8: With him were the bones of the livestock; and with us was our God, who helped us and fought for us in our battles. The people listened to the words of Jehoshua, the king of Judah.
verses.9: After that, Sanherib, king of Assyria, sent his servants to Jerusalem. He took control of Jerusalem and all its surrounding areas. He also took control over Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and over all of Judah, who were living in Jerusalem.
verses.10: So said Sanherib, king of Assyria: “Why do you trust in your strength and sit in the city of Jerusalem?”
verses.11: Do not let them strengthen themselves, so that they may lead you to death through hunger and cold. May the LORD our God save us from the power of King Assyria.
verses.12: He will remove their idols and their worship idols. He said to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before one of these idols is sacrificed, you must worship it and offer sacrifices to it.”
verses.13: You do not know what I and my ancestors have done for all the nations of the earth. The gods of those nations could not save their lands from my hands.
verses.14: Who among these gods of the nations is able to save his people from me? After all, your gods can surely save you from me.
verses.15: And now, let me not lead you away from Hizkiah. Let me not make you afraid of him either. Do not believe him; for no god or king can save his people from my hands, just as my ancestors could not save you from my hands either.
verses.16: And their servants also spoke about Jehovah, the God, and about Jehizkiah, his servant.
verses.17: And the books were written for to be a warning to Jehovah, the God of Israel. It was said that “like the gods of the other nations who did not save their people from my hands, so also will not the god of Yehoshia’ah save his people from my hands.”
verses.18: And they cried out loudly in Hebrew, “Hurry up! The people of Jerusalem must be taken captive and brought to destruction, so that the city can be captured.”
verses.19: And they said to the gods of Jerusalem, “They are like the gods of the people of the earth; they are works of human hands.”
verses.20: And Jehizkiah, the king, and Ishmael, son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed for this purpose. And the heavens cried out in sorrow.
verses.21: And Jehovah sent an angel, and all the rulers of the land were terrified. They said, “Let us flee to Egypt.” But Jehovah settled him in a place where there was no one around, and he entered the house of God. From there, he was thrown into the river.
verses.22: And the LORD saved Jehoshaphat and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hands of Sennacherib, the king of Assyria. And they were ruled by him from Sabtith.
verses.23: And many bring offerings to Jehovah in Jerusalem and from the cities of Judah’s king, Jehoshaphat. They also show them before all the nations from other places.
verses.24: In those days, Jehizkiah was sick until he died. He prayed to Jehovah and said, “May You give me hope.”
verses.25: And Jehizkiah did not forgive him. His heart was filled with anger, and he became furious over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.26: And Jehoshaphat humbled himself before God. But the people of Jerusalem did not come down upon them with wrath from Jehovah during Jehoshaphat’s reign.
verses.27: And Jehizkiah had great wealth and many treasures. He accumulated wealth in the form of silver, gold, precious stones, fabrics, and all kinds of valuable items.
verses.28: And for the dangers of breeding and inheritance, as well as for all kinds of diseases in both cattle and sheep, and also for wild animals.
verses.29: And he built cities for himself, and also a place for keeping sheep. He had plenty of food in the morning, for God had given him many treasures.
verses.30: And Hezekiah restored the ruins from the days of Jehoiakim, and he rebuilt them for the city of David. Hezekiah succeeded in all his endeavors.
verses.31: And also, in the prophecies of the kings of Babylon, who sent him to ask for punishment for the evil that he had done on earth. God left him there to test him and to see everything in his heart.
verses.32: And the additional words of Jehoshua and his kindnesses are written in the Book of the Prophets, by the prophet Amos, regarding the list of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.33: And Jehoshiaah was buried with his ancestors. He was buried above the tombs of the sons of David. All of Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him after his death. Menashe, his son, became king after him.
